description: Don't rewrite it in Rust. Rewrite the 5% that's slow: profile your app, port the hot functions with your coding agent, prove they behave the same. Python, JS/TS, Ruby, Java, Kotlin, Go, PHP, C/C++, C#, R.

latest_release.name: v0.9.0
latest_release.body:
- `scan --android <package>`: ranks an Android app's own methods on a device with adb + simpleperf, with device and build metadata; the report shows it as on-device (ART) evidence (#136).
- `scan --explain`: says what a scan would profile (language, runtime, Android modules and their layout) without running the app (#136).
- `scan --calibrate`: times the app without the profiler and shows the profiler's overhead (#142).
- `scan` keeps what the app printed in `.fast/app.log` (#142).
- Node: a low-attribution scan says where the rest of the run went (#164).
- README rewritten; demo GIFs show the current output.

Thanks @JuggyBob and @brixtonpham.

detail.readme:
Don't rewrite it in Rust. Rewrite the 5% that's slow.

Most of an app's runtime sits in a few functions. **fast-anything** finds them, has your coding agent port *only those* to Rust, proves the port returns the same results on real recorded calls, and swaps it in. Reversible, one function at a time.

## Install ```sh npm i -g @el4cteo/fast-anything # or: cargo install fast-anything ``` The command is `fast-anything`. Scanning needs only your app's runtime; porting needs Rust ([rustup](https://rustup.rs)). `fast-anything doctor` checks both. ## Use ```sh fast-anything go --agent claude -- python app.py ``` Use the command you normally run your app with (`node app.ts`, `go run .`, `gradle run`, `dotnet run`, …). `--agent` takes `claude`, `codex` or any command that reads a prompt on stdin. Step by step: | command | what it does | |---|---| | `scan -- ` | profiles the app and ranks functions by time and portability | | `port [id]` | records real calls and creates a one-function Rust crate with a `TASK.md` | | `verify` | builds the port and replays every recorded call against it | | `enable` / `disable` | switches the Rust in or out | | `bench` | times the whole app, original vs Rust, with an A/A noise control | | `report` | markdown + SVG card for your PR | | `status` / `doctor` | where things stand / what's installed | Useful `scan` flags: `--duration 30` for servers and GUIs, `--calibrate` to measure the profiler's overhead, `--explain` to check the setup without running. Every command takes `--json`. ## Proof, not vibes

- Every port is replayed against up to 500 real calls, plus edge cases (NaN, ±infinity, -0.0, empty, non-ASCII, bigger inputs) answered by the original. - Every 5th call is held out from the agent, so a port can't special-case what it was shown. - Nothing is enabled until all cases match, and a port that's slower per call stays off. - `FAST_ANYTHING_DISABLE=1` runs the original any time. ## Results Real runs on an i5-10500, Windows 11 (C and C++: a GitHub Actions Linux runner). Reproduce them from [`examples/`](examples). | app | before | after | |---|---|---| | Python fuzzy dedupe | 4.91s | **42ms, 116×** | | PHP fuzzy dedupe | 2.94s | **53ms, 55×** | | Go fuzzy dedupe | 3.02s | **144ms, 21×** | | TypeScript fuzzy dedupe | 3.11s | **155ms, 20×** | | Ruby fuzzy dedupe | 3.13s | **228ms, 14×** | | C# fuzzy dedupe | 4.03s | **312ms, 13×** | | C mandelbrot | 431ms | **127ms, 3.4×** | | Java fuzzy dedupe | 3.50s | **1.18s, 3×** (11× on the function; the rest is JVM startup) | | C++ fuzzy dedupe | 3.02s | **1.09s, 2.7×** | It ports the outermost loop it can, so the app crosses into Rust once instead of millions of times. ## Languages | language | how it's run | |---|---| | Python 3.10+ | `python app.py` (PyO3) | | JavaScript / TypeScript | `node` 22+, `bun`, `deno run -A` (napi-rs) | | Ruby 3.3+ | `ruby app.rb` | | Java 22+ | `java App.java`, Maven, Gradle | | Kotlin/JVM | Gradle, `src/main/kotlin`, JDK 22+ | | Go 1.22+ | `go run .` | | PHP 8.1+ | `php app.php` (FFI extension) | | C / C++ | gcc, clang, icx/icpx | | C# / .NET 8+ | `dotnet run -c Release` | | R 4.0+ | `Rscript app.R` | Python and JS/TS use native bindings; the rest call the port through one C entry point, with no headers or extra tools. It ports top-level, deterministic functions that take plain data (numbers, strings, lists, maps, arrays). `scan` says why anything else can't move yet. ## Android Android apps run on ART, so they're profiled on the device instead: ```sh fast-anything scan --android com.example.app --duration 10 ``` It ranks the app's own methods with simpleperf over adb (debuggable or profileable build). Device measurements (`import gfxinfo`, `perfetto`, `simpleperf`, `json`) go in the report in their own section. Ranking only: Android code isn't ported, and ART times are never compared with host ones. ## Agents - **Claude Code**: `/plugin marketplace add EL4CTEO/fast-anything`, then `/plugin install fast-anything@fast-anything` - **Codex**: `codex plugin marketplace add EL4CTEO/fast-anything` - **MCP server** (any client): `claude mcp add fast-anything -- fast-anything mcp` - **Skill**: [`skills/fast-anything`](skills/fast-anything/SKILL.md) teaches any agent the loop ## Sponsors fast-anything is free and open source. If it saves you time, sponsoring keeps it maintained.
